findings.what: Skip guard uses lexicographic string comparison `unicodedata.unidata_version < "13.0"`.
findings.why: String comparison is wrong for versions below 10: "9.0" < "13.0" is False, so on a Unicode 9.0 build the test would not skip and would crash on unicodedata.name() instead of skipping. Correctly skips for the realistic near-13.0 versions ("10.x"–"12.1"). Practically unreachable: the codebase requires Python 3.10+ (zip(strict=...), `X | None`), which ships Unicode >= 14.0, so the guard never fires in any runnable environment.
findings.fix: Compare with a proper version tuple, e.g. `tuple(map(int, unicodedata.unidata_version.split('.'))) < (13, 0)`.

renderer_invariants: all six hold — render size (cols*cell_w, rows*cell_h) verified; pure and deterministic (no module-level mutable state beyond the import-time registry); _on_dots only reads grid/palette and render_frame copies its background; cell_aspect = sx/sy; names unique and stable (registered under geometry names, duplicate raise verified); style.options JSON round-trip enforced by RenderStyle.__post_init__.
notes: Sextant blocker verified FIXED: table rebuilt and checked against the actual Unicode database (unidata 16.0) — 0 mismatches across all 60 expressible patterns, mask bit k == dot k+1 (row-major identity). Missing set {0,21,42,63} maps to U+0020 / U+1FB06 (SEXTANT-123, 3-dot) / U+1FB0A (SEXTANT-124, 3-dot) / U+2588; stand-ins are in-block 3-dot glyphs, never 2-dot. test_sextant_table_matches_unicode_names derives masks from names and the single-dot positional guards, so a transposed (column-major) table fails — genuine non-self-blessing test, and it runs (not skipped) on this build. Degenerate palette -> all-False dots -> EMPTY codepoint, consistent with _coverage_table returning zeros (coverage 0 = no ink). Owned tests independently run: 48 passed, 0 skipped. Minor docstring imprecision: 'upper two-thirds blocks' for SEXTANT-123/124 is loose (they are 3-dot approximations, dots {1,2,3}/{1,2,4}), but the essential '3-dot, never 2-dot' claim is correct.
